what: DOES A DIRECTION-AGNOSTIC ENTRY AT 5m LEVEL BREAKS CARRY A NET TIMING EDGE, OR IS IT BRACKET/COST GEOMETRY UNDER A DRIFTING WINDOW? (2026-11-19, QUEUE-FILL-STANDING-W47b, from RQ-20261119-d7c3-03 run 44442962409). MEASURED, DEV 2025-11-01..2026-09-15, six USDT perps, 28,059 level_break_break firings: S3 is NET of the full cost stack as registered (fee 11 bps round trip + slippage 3 bps + funding 1 bp/window through execution_costs.roundtrip_cost_r in desk_gen_replay_driver.simulate; no separate spread term). The random-side control reads +0.078 R, fade +0.088 R (lb +0.051), continuation +0.067 R (lb +0.024), so direction adds about +0.01 R and the effect is WHEN, not WHICH WAY. BUT both arms are deeply negative in absolute terms: mean net R of the fade firings -0.446 vs B3 mean -0.533 (n 28,059): S3 is 'less negative than random', not a profit. Candidate mechanism, UNVERIFIED: cost in R = bps / (1.5 x ATR14 as bps of price), so a firing bar whose ATR% sits higher inside its ATR%-decile than the matched random cutoffs pays less cost per R; the decile match (10 bins) leaves that room. Same sign on synthetic driftless data (random-side +0.057), where no timing edge can exist. FALSIFIER: re-run the random-side test (a) at 20-50 ATR% bins, and (b) cost-free (gross R) S3; if S3 shrinks toward 0 with finer matching or the gross S3 is about 0, it is cost-in-R geometry and nothing is filed further; if the net timing S3 survives on a later window (2026-09-15 onward, once enough has accrued) and at symmetric brackets, it is a timing edge.
